text:
maya: Quick question — after the kernel-selection tweak we shipped yesterday I'm seeing p99 spikes on Dedicated nodes in the 2–5s range for some tails. Repro is flaky. Anyone seen this pattern or have suggestions on a benchmark matrix to pin down whether it's a kernel scheduling issue, batching heuristic, or KV cache warmup?

raj: I saw similar on staging, mainly for long sequences. p95 moved a little but p99 jumped. My hunch: microbatch sizing + kernel choice creates convoying for rare long seqs. Also check KV cache hit-rate during the run.

olivia: Agree with raj. We should split tests by seq-length buckets (<=128, 129-512, >512) and by cache state (cold/warm). Tail often comes from cold-KV + kernel fallback.

li: For methodology: do both replay (real traffic) and targeted synthetic. Replay tells you realistic concurrency/arrival patterns. Synthetic lets you isolate variables (e.g., single long seq with background short ones).

maya: Thinking test matrix:
- Replay with 1h trace (live) at 100% QPS
- Replay headroom 1.5x to trigger batching differences
- Synthetic steady-state at fixed qps (microbatch sweep: 1,2,4,8)
- Cold-cache ramp tests
- Kernel-only microbench (no batching) to baseline kernel latency

raj: +measure per-token latency and per-kernel time. Add KV cache-hit tagging so we can break tails into cache-miss vs cache-hit.

olivia: Small loadgen snippet I used:
```
loadgen --trace ./captures/2026-03-15.trace --scale 1.5 --bucket-by seq_len --microbatch-sizes 1,2,4,8 --tag kv_state
```
Works well to reproduce convoying.

li: Also: be careful how we compute p99. If you aggregate across seq lengths you hide distributional effects. Use stratified p95/p99 per bucket and global percentiles weighted by request count.

maya: Good point. Should we report p99_end_to_end vs p99_kernel? End-to-end includes queuing which is what customers see.

raj: Both. Bug root cause can be either kernel slowdown or queuing. If kernel p99 is flat but end-to-end p99 jumps with microbatch increase, it's queuing/convoying.

perf-bot: Perf test run queued: job/1960001234-microbatch-sweep started on cluster-dedicated-3.

olivia: One more data point — in my replay runs, KV cache warming took ~6 minutes and that tail >99.9 for cold->warm transition. We should add a warmup window and report both warm and cold slices.

li: For signal hygiene, recommend storing per-request metadata: seq_len, microbatch_id, kernel_variant, kv_hit boolean, start/end timestamps. Then you can pivot.

maya: Action items:
- raj: run microbatch sweep + kernel microbench, collect per-request metadata
- olivia: run 2 replays (100% and 1.5x) with cold/warm variants
- li: add stratified p95/p99 and export simple notebook for triage
- I'll collate results and we can decide rollback vs tweak heuristic

raj: I'll start a run now and post logs. If anyone wants access to the trace, @maya I'll share s3 link.

olivia: :thumbsup: thanks

maya: Thanks all — let's reconvene tomorrow @10 to review raw tails.
